author: BBC News
description:
A Massachusetts jury are deliberating in the shocking case of Lindsay Clancy, a mother who admits to killing her three young children amid suffering, her lawyers argue, extreme post-partum psychosis. 

Online sleuths have been streaming the trial, and aggregating clips online to advance unfounded and defamatory conspiracies in the name of activism and awareness. 

Matt and Marianna explain how these creators operate, and consider the broader risks connected with the growing phenomenon of TikTok trials, from Depp v Heard to Karen Read.

00:00 Part One - Lindsay Clancy and the Online Courtroom

18:54 Part Two - The Rise of the Social Media Trial

description:
There are fears of more flash floods in Nepal, as rescuers scramble through villages engulfed in rock and mud in a desperate search for survivors of the flash floods that have left at least 1,400 missing and hundreds dead.  It is feared that the final death toll may be much higher. 

Survivors have been giving harrowing accounts of how their entire families were wiped away in the catastrophe. 

Hundreds of foreign nationals are desperately waiting to hear from loved ones thought to be caught in the disaster. Nepalese authorities say at least 380 people are confirmed to have died. 

The region is popular with trekkers from around the world and is a pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, visited by tens of thousands of pilgrims each year.

Travellers from at least 28 countries, are among those missing following the catastrophe, including many from India, China, the US, Canda, Australia, the UK and Japan.

description:
Meta’s agreed to an $18 billion settlement resolving claims from 29 US states that Facebook and Instagram harmed children.

Technology and AI editor Zoe Kleinman joins Adam Fleming to discuss the short trial and why Meta have settled and not admitted any wrongdoing. New features will be implemented on Facebook and Instagram for children including two-hour daily time limits and a night mode - but Meta says other tech platforms should be made to adopt these features too.

And, the Home Office has released its latest figures showing small boat arrivals have dropped by 23% on the previous year, along with a breakdown of other immigration statistics. Dominic Casciani, Home and Legal correspondent unpacks the story behind the latest migration statistics.

description:
Every time you ask ChatGPT a question, stream a film, save a photo to the cloud or join a video call, a data centre helps make it happen. 

But what happens when one of those facilities is planned for your community?  

In Cardiff, there is a proposal to turn a hospital park and ride site into a new data centre campus. Supporters say projects like this could bring jobs, investment and help power the UK's AI boom. Critics worry about transport, noise, energy use and the impact on their community. 

As demand for AI grows, more data centres are being planned across the UK. So where should they be built, who benefits, and what are the trade-offs?
